peers.name: skill-creator
peers.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

peers.name: pptx
peers.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions \"deck,\" \"slides,\" \"presentation,\" or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

peers.name: pdf
peers.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.

peers.name: docx
peers.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.

en.tagline: Distinct visual design for new or existing UI
en.summary: Guidance for designing UI with a distinct visual identity instead of template defaults. It covers aesthetic direction, typography, layout, and copy, and asks the agent to plan and review before writing code. The aim is a design that fits the brief's subject and does not look like a generated page.
problem: Generated UI often looks the same across unrelated products. It tends to repeat the same palette, card grid, eyebrow labels, and gradient accents whatever the subject is.

With this skill, the agent first identifies the subject, audience, and main job of the product. Palette, type, and layout choices then follow from that brief, and the plan is checked for generic defaults before any code is written.
fit: Building a new landing page or app screen from a brief
Restyling an existing UI that looks like a template
Choosing typefaces, a type scale, and a color palette
unfit: Brief already fixes every visual detail and leaves no room for choices
Matching an existing design system exactly
steps: If the brief does not name the subject, the agent proposes one concrete subject, audience, and primary job and confirms it with the client.
The agent writes a short plan with 4 to 6 named hex colors, the typefaces and their roles, a layout concept with ASCII wireframes, and alignment choices.
It reviews the plan against the brief and revises any part that reads as a generic default, noting what changed and why.
It writes the code from the revised plan, watching CSS selector specificity so that rules do not cancel each other out.
It critiques the build, using screenshots if the environment supports them, and removes decoration that does not serve the brief.
It checks the quality floor: responsive layout, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion, and accessible contrast.

zh.tagline: 为新建或现有界面做有辨识度的视觉设计
zh.summary: 这是一套界面视觉设计指南，目标是让界面有自己的风格，而不是套用模板。内容包括审美方向、字体、版面和文案。代理在写代码前会先做方案并自我审查。结果应贴合需求的主题，而不像生成的通用页面。
problem: 生成的界面常常彼此很像。不论产品是什么，它们往往用同样的配色、卡片网格、小标签和渐变装饰。
使用这个技能后，代理先确定产品的主题、受众和主要用途。配色、字体和版面的选择都从这份需求出发，并且在编码前检查方案是否落入通用默认样式。
fit: 根据需求从零做新的落地页或应用界面
重新设计一个看起来像模板的现有界面
选择字体、字号层级和配色
unfit: 需求已经把每个视觉细节定死，没有选择的余地
必须完全遵循既有设计系统
steps: 如果需求没有说明主题，代理会提出一个具体的主题、受众和主要用途，并请客户确认。
代理写出一份简短方案，包括 4 到 6 个有名称的十六进制颜色、字体及其用途、带 ASCII 线框的版面构思，以及对齐方式。
代理对照需求审查方案，修改任何看起来像通用默认的部分，并说明改了什么、为什么改。
代理按修改后的方案编写代码，注意 CSS 选择器的优先级，避免规则互相抵消。
代理检查成品，如果环境支持就截图审看，并去掉对需求没有帮助的装饰。
代理确认基本质量：响应式布局、可见的键盘焦点、尊重减少动效的设置，以及足够的颜色对比度。
